skills.name: build

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development

skills.name: gdb-debugging

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting

skills.name: user-app-development

105.     ///
106.     /// # Safety
107.     ///
108.     /// Behavior is undefined if the provided memory-mapped I/O address is invalid.
109.     ///
110.     // Identity wrapping that deliberately bypasses the physical-RAM-range validator: MMIO
111.     // addresses may legally lie outside tracked RAM. On success the abstract address is unchanged.
112.     #[verus_spec(result =>
113.         requires
114.             spec_frame_number(addr@) <= spec_max_frame_number(),
115.         ensures
116.             result is Ok,
117.             (result->Ok_0)@ == addr@,
118.             (result->Ok_0).inv(),
119.     )]
120.     pub unsafe fn from_mmio_address(addr: VirtualAddress) -> Result<Self, Error> {
121.         Ok(Self(addr))
122.     }
123. 
124.     ///
125.     /// # Description
126.     ///
127.     /// Constructs a [`PhysicalAddress`] from a [`FrameNumber`].
128.     ///
129.     /// # Parameters
130.     ///
131.     /// - `frame`: The frame number.
132.     ///
133.     /// # Returns
134.     ///
135.     /// A [`PhysicalAddress`] associated with the given `frame_number`.
136.     ///
137.     // Total constructor: the result is the frame's base address, hence `FRAME_SIZE`-aligned.
138.     #[verus_spec(result =>
139.         ensures
140.             result@ == spec_from_number(spec_frame_raw_value(frame)),
141.     )]
142.     pub fn from_number(frame: FrameNumber) -> Self {
143.         proof! { lemma_from_number_no_overflow(frame); }
144.         let addr: usize = frame.into_raw_value() * mem::FRAME_SIZE;
145.         Self(VirtualAddress::new(addr))
146.     }
147. 
148.     // Total projection (under `inv()`): identifies the frame containing the address,
149.     // `self@ / FRAME_SIZE` (equivalently `self@ >> FRAME_SHIFT`). `inv()` underwrites the unwrap.
150.     #[verus_spec(result =>
151.         requires
152.             self.inv(),
153.         ensures
154.             spec_frame_raw_value(result) == spec_frame_number(self@),
155.     )]
156.     pub fn into_frame_number(self) -> FrameNumber {
157.         let raw_addr: usize = self.0.into_raw_value();
158.         // Bind `FRAME_SHIFT` once so the proof relates the shift below to the same value.
159.         let shift: usize = mem::FRAME_SHIFT;
160.         let frame_number: usize = raw_addr >> shift;
161.         proof! { lemma_frame_index(self, raw_addr, shift, frame_number); }
162.         // Safety: the following unwrap is safe because a physical address has a valid frame number.
163.         FrameNumber::from_raw_value(frame_number).unwrap()
164.     }
